accuracy.evidence: Every value was checked by hand in eighths: the data set 1½, 1¾, 1⅝, 1¼, 1 4/8, 1 6/8, 1⅞, 1 2/4 gives stacks of 3 at 1½ (4/8), 2 at 1¾, and 1 each at 1¼, 1⅝ and 1⅞; four values are greater than 1½; 1⅞ − 1¼ = 7/8 − 2/8 = 5/8; 1½ × 3 = 4½. Mastery items were recomputed (1¾ − 1⅜ = 6/8 − 3/8 = 3/8; 3 × 1¼ = 3¾; 1⅜ to 1⅞ is 4/8 = ½). Standards wording matches Common Core 4.MD.B.4 and 5.MD.B.2 and the England Year 4/5 fractions and statistics statements.

misconceptions.evidence: The predictions, scene feedback and challenge target documented fraction errors: a larger denominator means a larger piece (scene 1 prediction, challenge 'big8'), equivalent forms plotted apart (scene 2 prediction, 1 4/8 and 1 2/4 cards, challenge 'equiv'), counting marks instead of gaps (6/8 key in scene 4, challenge 'marks'), adding or subtracting both numerators and denominators (6/4 and 3 3/6 keys, challenge 'tops'), and counting equal values as greater (7 key in scene 3, challenge 'incl'). The adult text names all five.

lab_distinct.evidence: The lab is about fractional measurement scales: a scale that names only 1, 1½ and 2 so quarter and eighth marks must be reasoned out, data cards written in equivalent forms that must share a stack, a difference found by counting eighth jumps with arcs drawn, and 1½ inch bars laid end to end on a quarter-marked ruler. It differs from flaglplot (whole centimetres, ages 7–8) and flaghist; the shingle gate found under 30% overlap with every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner finds out before being told: tapping 1¼ at the 4th mark gets 'each quarter is 2 eighths', so the eighths structure is discovered; placing 1 4/8 away from 1½ is refused with the reason, so equivalence is felt on the line; after both Xs are picked, the 5 drawn arcs make the difference countable before the keys appear; laying three bars shows the total reaching 4½ on the ruler before the learner chooses it. Done messages only confirm.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: '⅛ inch, because 8 is bigger' (the scale shows ⅛ is half of ¼), 'in two different places' for 1 2/4 and 1 4/8 (they land in one stack), 'take away tops and bottoms: 6/4' (the arcs show 5 eighths), and '3/6' for ½ + ½ + ½ (the ruler shows 1½ per three halves). The reveal line names the right answer after each task.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with eight feedback messages keyed to the slip: big8 (more pieces means smaller pieces, ¼ = 2/8), equiv (1 4/8 joins the 1½ stack), marks (count jumps, 4 jumps = ½), tops (keep the bottom number), incl ('taller than' leaves out equal values), whole (add wholes and fractions, ¾ + ¾ = 1½), add (minus means take away) and a general eighths reminder. Scene keys also explain each wrong choice, e.g. 6/8 says 'you counted the marks from 1¼ to 1⅞'.

readability.evidence: Learner kid paragraphs use short sentences and name one idea each (eighths, stacking Xs, counting gaps, adding wholes then fractions) and pass the learner kid limit; adult text passes the adult limit in validate_lessons.py. Canvas prompts are under 10 words ('Tap 1¾ on the scale (2 of 4)'). Fractions are shown as ⅛ ¼ ⅜ ½ glyphs on the scale so labels stay short on a phone.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph teaches one step of the method, and the adult text gives the standards, the method in eighths, the five named mistakes and what the lab asks. The content gate found no filler phrases and under 12% overlap with every other lesson, including 723 (whole-centimetre line plots) and 434 (dot plots).

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 dark, 360 px Android light and desktop light screenshots part-way through each Show me: all nine scale labels (1, 1⅛ … 2) fit at 360 px without overlap, stacks of 3 Xs stay clear of the seedling card, the 5-jump arcs and their label sit between the keys and the Xs, the 0–5 inch ruler shows half labels above the ticks with the bars above them, and number keys are over 44 px tall.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a labelled button twin: a pointer moved with '◀ Left' and 'Right ▶' plus 'Pick this mark', 'Place the X here', 'Pick this height' and 'Pick this X'; the count, difference and total keys ('Difference ⅝ inch'); and 'Lay a bar'. Each result is spoken through c.say and the canvas aria-label (the pointer reports 'Pointer at 1⅜ inches'), challenge feedback is in a polite live region, and right or wrong is stated in words. The walk gate's axe run was clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
